get.description:
One job's full detail — status, attempts, last error, payload — the see-before-you-act read
behind replay and cancel: an operator decides whether to replay from WHY it failed. A platform
operator sees any job; a tenant reader is scoped to its own, and a job it may not see reads as
absent (404) rather than revealing that it exists.

post.description:
Deliver one batch of due jobs on every push-enabled queue. Driven by the SAME central ticker
that calls scheduler/tick and jobs/reclaim — so no consuming service needs its own CronJob. A
no-op when push is disabled.

post.description:
Register (or replace) the PUSH webhook for a queue. From now, that queue's due jobs are
delivered by job-service POSTing each to `url`, instead of the target polling claim(). The host
must be egress-allow-listed (SSRF). A queue with no target stays PULL — this is purely additive.

post.description:
A worker leases up to `batch` due jobs (atomic; each carries a lease_token). A worker may pass
`tenant` to restrict its leases to that tenant when a queue is shared across tenants (job-004).

schema.title: Response Claim Internal Jobs Claim Post

post.description:
Any service enqueues background work. Idempotent on idempotency_key / unique_key.

TRUST BOUNDARY (job-004): `tenant` is caller-supplied, not derived from the internal caller
assertion, so a holder of the internal token can stamp a job with any tenant. This is acceptable
only because the internal tier is a trusted service mesh gated by the internal token + per-route
policy. Cross-tenant job DELIVERY is defended on the claim side: a worker passes its own tenant to
/jobs/claim to lease only its tenant's jobs, so a shared queue name cannot leak work between
tenants even if a peer mis-stamps one. Prefer per-tenant queues where isolation must be absolute.
